title: Best Grass Trimmers and Strimmers UK
short: Cordless, corded and petrol grass trimmers compared for cutting power, noise and battery life, tested on real grass, weeds and brambles in a home garden.
intro: A grass trimmer's real test is how it copes with rough patches, weeds and brambles, not a neatly mown demo lawn. This guide compares trimmers tested by Expert Reviews in their own garden, measuring noise levels and hand-arm vibration at the handle, and timing cordless battery life during actual cutting.

products.name: UniversalGrassCut 18V-26-500
products.best_for: Buyers who want strong all-round performance and a widely compatible battery system
products.key_spec: 18V, 26cm cutting width, 4-position adjustable head rotating 180° for edging, 20-minute battery life
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this the best strimmer in its class for whacking chunky thistles and tough nettles, with flawless line management that lets you squeeze the trigger and let it get on with the job. Its Power For All batteries also work in tools from Flymo, Husqvarna and Gardena, though it's a little head-heavy and battery life could be better, offsetting with a fast 1hr 15min recharge.
pros: Great cutting performance on tough weeds
cons: Battery life could be better (20 minutes)

products.name: AdvancedGrassCut 36
products.best_for: Buyers with larger, rougher gardens who don't want a petrol trimmer
products.key_spec: 36V, 30cm cutting width, 40-minute battery life, Power For All battery compatibility
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this has more power than the average cordless trimmer, tackling a big-sized plot with a wide 30cm cutting width and a respectable 40 minutes of cutting time. It's genuinely hard to find a cordless model with more raw grass-cutting and weed-chopping power, though most of the weight sits toward the cutting head and there's no harness included.
pros: Great cutting power for tough, rough grass
Battery shared across Bosch, Husqvarna, Gardena and Flymo tools
cons: A little on the heavy side

products.name: RY18LT23A-0
products.best_for: Budget buyers who want a light, easy-to-use trimmer for everyday jobs
products.key_spec: 18V, 23cm cutting width, 2kg, 73-minute battery life measured in no-load tests
products.summary: Expert Reviews found one of the cheapest cordless strimmers around still impressed on performance, lightweight at just 2kg and easy to wield without needing a harness. Battery life measured an impressive 73 minutes with the 4Ah battery, and the swivelling head handles edges well, though it's noisy and doesn't clear thicker clumps of grass or brambles as well as pricier models.
cons: Struggles with thick clumps and brambles

products.name: FSA 50
products.best_for: Buyers with close neighbours who need a genuinely quiet trimmer
products.key_spec: 18V, 26cm cutting width, 78dBA noise measured, 2.9mm/sec vibration measured, 42-minute battery life
products.summary: Expert Reviews measured this as one of the quietest strimmers ever tested, at just 78dBA, and vibration of a barely-there 2.9mm/sec, well within government hand-arm vibration exposure guidelines even for all-day use. Battery life measured 42 minutes with superb adjustability for tall and short gardeners alike, though the line is prone to breakage and the trigger operation is fiddly.
pros: Very low measured vibration, safe for all-day use

products.name: Contour 500E
products.best_for: Buyers with a small garden who want a cheap, no-fuss trimmer
products.key_spec: 500W motor, 25cm cutting width, 10m mains cable, wire plant guard
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this a serious step up from its predecessor with an extra 200W of power and an adjustable handle, making it the best-value option currently tested. It whizzed through rougher, tougher grass and weedy areas in testing, and a wire plant guard protected surrounding plants from damage, though the mains cord limits convenience versus cordless models.
pros: Lightweight with a comfortable adjustable handle
Good cutting power for rougher grass and weeds
cons: Mains cord limits range and convenience

products.name: ST1511E-T 38cm Line Trimmer
products.best_for: Buyers who want petrol-level power without the petrol
products.key_spec: 56V 2.5Ah battery, 38cm cutting width, two speeds, 49-minute battery life measured
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this made light work of tough clumps of grass better than any strimmer their reviewer had ever tested, slicing through brambles as if they weren't there. The chunky 2.4mm nylon twist line rarely snapped once installed, and the 56V battery provided around 49 minutes of working time in testing, though it's expensive at £359.
pros: Cuts through brambles with petrol-level power
Two speeds for tough or delicate areas
cons: Line can be hard to thread

products.name: FS40
products.best_for: Large, overgrown gardens where cordless power isn't enough
products.key_spec: 2-stroke petrol engine, 38cm cutting width, optional 3-tooth poly-cut head for thick undergrowth
products.summary: Expert Reviews found the two-stroke engine provided plenty of power for a genuinely overgrown garden, with an optional three-tooth poly-cut head available for thicker undergrowth and brush the standard line can't handle. It's easier to start than most petrol trimmers with a simple bump-feed line mechanism, though at 2.9kg with the motor at the end of the stalk, it's not manageable for everyone.
pros: Excellent weed and undergrowth clearing power
Optional brush cutter blade for thick vegetation

guide.q: Cordless, corded or petrol: which type of trimmer do I need?
guide.a: A corded trimmer like the Flymo Contour 500E here is cheap and powerful but limited by cable range, best for small gardens. A cordless model like the Bosch UniversalGrassCut here gives freedom of movement for most garden sizes. A petrol trimmer like the Stihl FS40 suits very large or heavily overgrown gardens where cordless power and battery life aren't enough.

guide.q: How much power do I actually need?
guide.a: For cordless trimmers, 18V models like the Bosch UniversalGrassCut or Ryobi here suit small to medium gardens and light work, while 36V or higher, like the Bosch AdvancedGrassCut, copes with heavier workloads without bogging down in scrub. For corded trimmers, look for 500W or above for anything beyond light trimming.

It can save real money. Bosch's Power For All batteries, used on the UniversalGrassCut and AdvancedGrassCut here, also work in tools from Flymo, Husqvarna and Gardena, so if you already own a compatible tool or plan to buy more garden equipment, sharing one battery system across brands avoids buying multiple battery packs.

guide.q: How much do noise and vibration actually matter?
guide.a: A lot, if you'll be trimming for long periods or have close neighbours. Expert Reviews measured the Stihl FSA 50 here at just 78dBA with vibration low enough to meet government all-day exposure guidelines, a genuine step up in comfort over noisier, more vibration-prone budget models.
